gaps.sentence: They said nothing at all, ___ I found rather strange.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' here means 'and this'; it refers to the whole situation and follows a comma.

gaps.sentence: The bridge, on ___ repairs are still continuing, will reopen in May.
gaps.explanation: 'On which' is the formal pattern; 'where' cannot follow a preposition, and 'that' is barred from non-defining clauses.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ hand in their essays late will lose marks.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to the students performing the action; the verb 'will lose' follows later in the sentence.

gaps.sentence: My uncle, ___ lives in Canada, is coming to stay next week.
gaps.hint: non-defining clause after a comma about a person
gaps.explanation: In non-defining clauses (between commas) 'that' is not allowed; 'who' refers to people.

gaps.sentence: The children were amazed by ___ they saw at the circus.
gaps.explanation: 'What they saw' means 'the things that they saw'; after the preposition 'by' only a nominal clause like this fits.

gaps.sentence: The reason ___ I'm calling is to confirm your appointment.
gaps.explanation: 'The reason why' introduces the explanation or cause; the other options do not express reason.

gaps.sentence: July and August are the months ___ most Italians take their holidays.
gaps.explanation: 'When' means 'in which' after time expressions; the clause describes when the action happens.

gaps.sentence: The shower suddenly stopped working, ___ meant we had to call a plumber.
gaps.hint: refers back to the whole event
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to the whole preceding clause; 'what' cannot introduce this kind of clause after a comma.
